findings.F1: Across all six coins, a daily drop of 1 to 2 times the coin's 20-day volatility is followed by a next-day excess return of +0.42% (t=3.03, n=1276 one-day cases, 58% up), every bucket with a drop of 1 sigma or more rises the next day 58-61% of the time, and a rise of 1 sigma or more is followed by an up day only 41-47% of the time.
findings.F2: The next-day rebound after a drop of 1 sigma or more is larger when the close is below its SMA200, at +0.57% (t=3.29, n=1013, 59% up), than above it, at +0.25% (t=1.34, n=794); it is positive in all six coins (strongest in XMR, +0.84%, t=3.08, n=301) and in six of eight years (2020 t=2.61, 2021 t=3.44), though it fades to about zero in 2024-2025.
findings.F3: Below the SMA200 the mirror image appears: a rise of 1 sigma or more is followed by a next-day excess of -0.28% (t=-1.77, n=782, only 43% up), against +0.16% (t=1.04, n=1102) above it.
findings.F4: The day after a Friday-dated bar has an excess return of +0.34% (t=4.32, n=2430, 54.5% up); it is positive in all six coins (LTC t=2.71, XMR t=2.07) and in seven of eight years, with t>2.4 in 2019, 2020, 2024 and 2025.
findings.F5: The day after a Wednesday-dated bar has an excess of -0.34% (t=-3.02, n=2437); it is negative in all six coins, but most of it comes from 2019 (t=-6.75), and no other year reaches |t|>1.4.
findings.F6: The tested depth signal does not rank outcomes: the 10-bar excess is -1.35% at forecast 2-5 (t=-1.32, n=139), -0.26% at 5-10 (n=99) and +2.17% at 10-20 (t=1.38, n=102); after forecast ≥2, 2020 alone gives +10.6% (t=6.08, n=21), while 2018-2019 are negative (-2.5%, -1.8%).
findings.F7: Trades entered at a shallow forecast of 1-3 earn +4.05% net on average over 45 days, against +1.54% over 17 days for entries at 8-21, with similar hit rates of 66-69% (n=115 and 596), so the book's gain comes from holding long through recoveries, not from the extreme-depth timing.
findings.F8: Coins in their top quintile of past 10-day return gain a further +1.87% excess over the next 10 bars (t=1.99, n=306 non-overlapping, 56% up), positive in all six coins, but it swings by year (2020 +8.2% t=4.15, 2018 -6.2% t=-1.93).

ideas.idea: When a coin trading below its 200-day average closes a day down by more than its usual daily move (at least one 20-day standard deviation), it rises the next day more often than on an ordinary day, because forced and panicked sellers in a downtrend overshoot and are absorbed within a day.
ideas.consequence: A trader can take a one-day long after an outsized down close below the SMA200, and avoid opening fresh shorts on that close.
ideas.name: downtrend sell-off next-day rebound

ideas.idea: When a coin trading below its 200-day average closes a day up by more than one 20-day standard deviation, the next day falls more often than an ordinary day, as rallies inside a downtrend are sold into.
ideas.consequence: A trader should refuse to chase a sharp up close below the SMA200 with a new long, and can fade it for a day.
ideas.name: downtrend rally next-day fade

ideas.idea: The daily bar that follows a Friday-dated bar (the weekend Saturday session) returns more than the coin's average day, reflecting thin weekend liquidity dominated by retail buyers.
ideas.consequence: A trader can favour holding or adding longs into the Saturday session and delay planned sells until after it.
ideas.name: Saturday weekend upward drift

ideas.idea: A coin whose 10-day return is in its own top fifth keeps outperforming its average drift over the next ten days, as late buyers extend visible moves.
ideas.consequence: A trader should hold rather than trim a coin after a strong 10-day run.
ideas.name: strong ten-day run continuation
